title: Arranmore Island Walk Route

images.title: Joseph Mischyshyn / Leabgarrow Harbour on Arranmore Island
images.caption: Leabgarrow Harbour on Arranmore Island. The island's flora and fauna are shaped by its Atlantic location and diverse habitats. The windswept moorlands are covered with heather, gorse, and mosses, which thrive in the harsh conditions. Coastal cliffs are home to seabirds such as puffins, razorbills, and fulmars, while inland areas provide habitat for songbirds like skylarks and meadow pipits. Grey seals are often spotted along the rocky shorelines, and dolphins and basking sharks can sometimes be seen in the surrounding waters during the summer months. The island’s wild beauty and diverse wildlife make it a haven for nature lovers and outdoor enthusiasts alike.

description: This walk explores Arranmore Island, the largest inhabited island of County Donegal. The walk starts at the ferry terminal and heads northwest across the island to the lighthouse, offering breathtaking views of the Atlantic Ocean and the rugged coastline. The route passes through small villages, quiet lanes, and open moorland, showcasing the island’s rich heritage and natural beauty. The lighthouse, perched on a cliff, marks a key navigational point and offers sweeping views of the surrounding sea and distant islands. Arranmore Island has a long history of habitation, with evidence of human activity dating back thousands of years. The island is home to a vibrant Gaelic-speaking community, and its culture and traditions are strongly rooted in music, storytelling, and seafaring. Visitors can still see remnants of its past, including old stone walls, famine-era ruins, and traces of ancient settlements scattered across the landscape. The island also played a role in maritime history, with its strategic location being essential for navigation and communication in the north Atlantic.

details.subtitle: Further Information and Other Local Ideas
details.content: On the mainland you can continue your walking on the Dungloe River Walk. You can also visit Bloody Foreland where there are fine cliff top trails and views of other nearby islands such as Tory Island.
